summary: A bris milah may be done on Shabbos, but may we bring the knife on Shabbos? Rabbi Eliezer allows even making the knife, but Rabbi Akiva says anything that could have been done before Shabbos may not be done on Shabbos.
stIntro: As a continuation to the discussion at the end of the previous chapter, which mentioned circumcision in the context of a discussion of the halakhot of childbirth on Shabbat, the mishna continues to address the halakhot of circumcision.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.he: אִם לֹא הֵבִיא כְלִי מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: if he did not bring the knife before Shabbos,
chunks.st: If he did not bring an implement for circumcising the child on Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: he brings it on Shabbos uncovered.
chunks.st: he brings it on Shabbat itself uncovered
chunks.stMore: so that it will be clear to all that he is bringing a circumcision scalpel.

chunks.en: And in a time of danger, he covers it in front of witnesses.
chunks.explain: When the government forbade doing a bris.
chunks.st: And in times of danger, when decrees of persecution prohibit Jews from circumcising their children, one covers it in the presence of witnesses
chunks.stMore: who can testify that he transported the scalpel to perform a mitzva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer also said,
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said with regard to this issue:

chunks.en: we may cut down trees to make charcoal
chunks.st: One may even cut down trees to prepare charcoal in order

chunks.en: to make an iron knife.
chunks.st: to fashion iron tools
chunks.stMore: for the purpose of circumcision. Rabbi Eliezer’s approach was not universally accepted, and

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said a rule:
chunks.st: a principle was stated by Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.en: Any melacha that could be done before
chunks.st: Any prohibited labor that can be performed on Shabbat eve

chunks.en: Shabbos does not push aside Shabbos,
chunks.st: does not override Shabbat, including transporting the circumcision scalpel. However, any prohibited labor involved in the mitzva of circumcision itself

chunks.en: and one that could not be done before
chunks.st: that cannot be performed on Shabbat eve

chunks.en: Shabbos pushes aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: overrides Shabbat.

summary: Everything needed for the bris milah itself may be done on Shabbos, including putting on a bandage and medicine. Whatever could have been prepared before Shabbos is done in a different way.
stIntro: When the eighth day of a baby’s life occurs on Shabbat, he must be circumcised on that day. Therefore,

chunks.en: We do everything needed for a bris milah on Shabbos:
chunks.st: one performs all the necessities of the circumcision, even on Shabbat:

chunks.en: we do the milah and the other steps of the bris,
chunks.st: One circumcises the foreskin, and uncovers
chunks.stMore: the skin by removing the thin membrane beneath the foreskin,

chunks.en: and we put a bandage and cumin on it.
chunks.st: and sucks the blood from the wound, and places on it both a bandage [ispelanit] and cumin as a salve.

chunks.en: If he did not grind the cumin before Shabbos,
chunks.st: If one did not grind the cumin from Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: he chews it with his teeth and puts it on.
chunks.st: he chews it with his teeth and places it on the place of circumcision as a salve.

chunks.en: If he did not mix wine
chunks.st: If he did not mix wine

chunks.en: and oil before Shabbos,
chunks.st: and oil on Shabbat eve,
chunks.stMore: a mixture designed to heal and strengthen the child,

chunks.en: each one is put on by itself.
chunks.st: this, the wine, is placed on the wound by itself and that, the oil, is placed by itself.

chunks.en: We may not make a covering for it from the start,
chunks.st: And on Shabbat one may not make a pouch to place over the circumcision as a bandage ab initio,

chunks.en: but he may wrap a rag around it.
chunks.st: but he may wrap a rag over it as a dressing.

chunks.en: If he did not prepare it before Shabbos,
chunks.st: If he did not prepare the bandage on Shabbat eve
chunks.stMore: by bringing it to the place where the circumcision was performed,

chunks.en: he wraps it around his finger and brings it,
chunks.st: he wraps the bandage on his finger and brings it on Shabbat,

chunks.en: even from another courtyard.
chunks.st: even from a different courtyard.
chunks.stMore: While the Sages permitted it to be brought, they required that it be performed in an unusual fashion, by wearing it in the manner of a garment.

summary: We may wash a baby on Shabbos before and after his bris, because he is in danger while it hurts. If we are not sure he needs a bris on that day, we may not break Shabbos for it.

chunks.en: We may wash the baby
chunks.st: One may wash the baby on Shabbat,

chunks.he: בֵּין לִפְנֵי הַמִּילָה וּבֵין לְאַחַר הַמִּילָה,
chunks.en: whether before the milah or after the milah,
chunks.st: both before the circumcision and after the circumcision.

chunks.en: and we may sprinkle water on him by hand,
chunks.st: And one may sprinkle hot water on him by hand

chunks.en: but not with a vessel.
chunks.st: but not with a vessel,
chunks.stMore: in order to depart from the usual manner in which this is done.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

chunks.en: we may wash the baby on the third day
chunks.st: One may wash the baby on the third day following his circumcision, even if

chunks.en: even when it falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: that third day occurs on Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: On the third day following circumcision, the baby is considered to be in danger,

chunks.en: as it says: "And it was
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to the men of Shekhem, who were circumcised: “And it came to pass

chunks.en: on the third day, when they were in pain."
chunks.st: on the third day, when they were in pain”
chunks.stMore: (Genesis 34:25). This teaches us that on the third day the pain of circumcision poses a danger. If there is

chunks.en: A baby we are not sure about, and an androginos: we do not break
chunks.st: uncertainty whether or not to circumcise a baby, and likewise in the case of a hermaphrodite [androginos]
chunks.stMore: baby, who possesses both male and female genitals,

words.note: A baby we cannot tell is a boy or a girl.

chunks.en: Shabbos for him.
chunks.st: one does not desecrate Shabbat
chunks.stMore: to perform the circumcision, since it is not certain that the circumcision is required.

chunks.en: But Rabbi Yehudah allows it for an androginos.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda permits doing so for a hermaphrodite baby.

summary: If a mohel by mistake did a bris on Shabbos for a baby whose bris was meant for another day, he did a melacha. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua argue when the bris was late.

chunks.en: Someone who had two babies,
chunks.st: One who had two babies to circumcise,

chunks.en: one to have a bris after Shabbos
chunks.st: one of whom he needed to circumcise on the day after Shabbat,

chunks.en: and one to have a bris on Shabbos,
chunks.st: and one of whom he needed to circumcise on Shabbat,

chunks.en: and he forgot and did the bris of the one
chunks.st: and he forgot and circumcised the one that should have been circumcised

chunks.en: for after Shabbos on Shabbos,
chunks.st: after Shabbat on Shabbat,

chunks.en: is chayav. One to have a bris on Erev Shabbos
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin-offering, because he performed the prohibited labor of causing a wound not in the framework of performing a mitzva, as no obligation yet exists to circumcise the child. If there were two babies, one to circumcise on Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: and one to have a bris on Shabbos,
chunks.st: and one to circumcise on Shabbat,

chunks.en: and he forgot and did the bris of the one
chunks.st: and he forgot and circumcised the one that he should have circumcised on

chunks.en: for Erev Shabbos on Shabbos:
chunks.st: Shabbat eve on Shabbat,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says he must bring a korban chatas,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable to bring a sin-offering,
chunks.stMore: as circumcision after its appointed time does not override Shabbat.

chunks.en: and Rabbi Yehoshua says he is patur.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehoshua exempts
chunks.stMore: him; since he intended to perform a mitzva, and despite his error in fact performed a mitzva, he is exempt from bringing a sin-offering.

summary: A baby usually has his bris on the eighth day, but sometimes it is pushed off to the ninth, tenth, eleventh, or twelfth day. A sick baby waits until he is healthy.

chunks.en: A baby has his bris at eight days,
chunks.st: a child is generally circumcised at eight
chunks.stMore: days, as the verse states: “And on the eighth day, the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised” (Leviticus 12:3), nevertheless, at times he is circumcised

chunks.en: at nine, and at ten,
chunks.st: at nine days, at times at ten days,

chunks.en: and at eleven,
chunks.st: at eleven days,

chunks.en: and at twelve,
chunks.st: and at twelve days,

chunks.en: not less and not more.
chunks.st: no earlier and no later.

chunks.en: How so?
chunks.st: How so?

chunks.en: The usual way, at eight.
chunks.st: In his usual manner, a child is circumcised at eight days. If

chunks.en: If he was born at twilight,
chunks.st: he was born at twilight
chunks.stMore: and it is therefore uncertain on which day he was born,

chunks.en: he has his bris at nine.
chunks.st: he is circumcised at nine
chunks.stMore: days, as his circumcision is postponed due to that uncertainty, as perhaps the eighth day from his birth has not yet arrived. If he was born

chunks.en: At twilight of Erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: at twilight on Shabbat eve,
chunks.stMore: he is not circumcised on the following Shabbat, due to the uncertainty whether it is the eighth or ninth day since his birth, and only a circumcision definitely performed at the appointed time overrides Shabbat. Rather, he is circumcised on Sunday, and the result is that

chunks.en: he has his bris at ten.
chunks.st: he is circumcised at ten days. If there was

chunks.en: If Yom Tov comes after that Shabbos,
chunks.st: a Festival after that Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: he is not circumcised on the Festival either, and

chunks.en: he has his bris at eleven.
chunks.st: he is circumcised at eleven days. And if that Shabbat was followed by

chunks.he: שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
chunks.en: The two days of Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah:
chunks.st: two days of Rosh HaShana, the result is that

chunks.en: he has his bris at twelve.
chunks.st: he is circumcised at twelve
chunks.stMore: days. The mishna states another halakha: With regard to

chunks.en: A sick baby:
chunks.st: a sick child,

chunks.en: we do not do his bris until he gets healthy.
chunks.st: one does not circumcise him until he becomes healthy.

summary: If part of the bris was not done properly, it must be finished, and until then the bris does not count. If it looks unfinished, it is fixed so people will not think it is wrong.

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ הֵן צִיצִין הַמְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמִּילָה,
chunks.en: These are the bits of skin that hold back the milah:
chunks.st: These are the shreds of flesh that invalidate the circumcision
chunks.stMore: if they are not cut. The essential element of circumcision is the removal of

chunks.en: if skin is left over most of the place of the bris.
chunks.st: the flesh that covers most of the corona,
chunks.stMore: and a child that was not circumcised in this manner is considered uncircumcised,

chunks.en: And he may not eat terumah.
chunks.explain: If he is a Kohen, his bris must be finished first.
chunks.st: and he does not eat teruma.

chunks.en: And if he had extra skin,
chunks.st: And if he was properly circumcised but he was fleshy,
chunks.stMore: and it appears as though he has not been properly circumcised, the circumcisor should

chunks.en: it is fixed so that it will not look wrong.
chunks.st: correct it by circumcising more than necessary, to avoid the appearance
chunks.stMore: of transgression, so he will not appear uncircumcised.

chunks.en: If he did the milah but did not finish the next step,
chunks.st: If one circumcised but did not uncover the flesh at the area of the circumcision
chunks.stMore: by folding back the thin membrane beneath the foreskin,

chunks.en: it is as if he did not do the milah.
chunks.st: it is as if he had not circumcised.
